solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Comedian in panic, I'm occasionally laid back

indicators.note: laid back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A comic performer who now and then panics, but mostly stays relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' without a job: it signals the run CIMOC inside 'panic, I'm occasionally', and 'laid back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a performer of jokes, a straightforward synonym for a comedian.

clue.text: Play with acts for all the actors!

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle about with it, so the letters of acts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage instruction: a play in several acts needs every member of the company.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a production is the full company of performers appearing in it.

clue.text: Spot former European currency

explanation.surface: Someone noticing an old coin from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark is both a blemish on a surface and the old German monetary unit, the Deutschmark.

clue.text: Certainly not a Tory boy, soldier possibly

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, i.e. a Tory
a boy is a son
a soldier is one kind of ant, so this is a definition by example

explanation.surface: Someone insisting a young soldier is no Conservative party lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'a' as the letter A: a vowel, so it is certainly not a consonant.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter A is a vowel, and a consonant is any letter that is not a vowel, so the clue's 'a' never is one.

clue.text: Drink after drink for champion

indicators.note: the first drink named comes after the second in the answer

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine, a drink

explanation.surface: A round of drinks, one after another, for the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to back or support it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cold-blooded fish occupying dirty home

indicators.note: the fish occupies the home, so it sits inside those letters

parts.note: a sty is a filthy dwelling, literally a pig's home
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded creature living in a filthy dwelling, as fish are cold-blooded.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely describes someone hard and unfeeling, which is what cold-blooded means of a person.

clue.text: Shortly, choose image

indicators.note: shortly says the word for choose is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: An instruction to select a picture soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Pic is informal shorthand for a picture, a photo or image.

clue.text: Certainly old, refocus after treatment

indicators.note: letters given treatment are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old patient sure to see better after eye treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is an idiomatic phrase of assent meaning certainly or naturally.

clue.text: It's ten, we suspect, for a decade

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Guessing the time is ten o'clock, alongside a reference to a period of years.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties is a ten-year span, such as the 1920s, so it names a decade.

clue.text: Odd mountains behind street

indicators.note: the mountains come behind, i.e. after, the street

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: An unusual view of hills rising beyond a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and odd are synonyms meaning unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: Store money, did you say?

indicators.note: the question asks about something spoken, so the word for money is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether they heard 'store money' correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store or hoard of goods, used as a noun synonym.

clue.text: Understand clubs, for example, do the same thing

parts.note: to follow an argument is to understand it
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card player working out that clubs must be played to match the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games following suit means playing the same suit as led, hence idiomatically copying what others do.

clue.text: Tiring, I saw more failing with low grade

indicators.note: failing means going wrong, so the letters are set out of order

parts.note: E is a low mark in a grading scale

explanation.surface: An exhausted student who saw more failing with a poor mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome describes something that wears you out, so it is a synonym for tiring.

clue.text: American in resort tailored garment

indicators.note: the American abbreviation sits in the rearranged letters
tailored means cut and sewn into shape, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: An American tourist at a holiday resort wearing made-to-measure clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are an item of clothing for the legs, so they are an example of a garment.

clue.text: Item ain't terribly close

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are set out badly, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A colloquial remark that some object is not especially near.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate friends are close ones, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Payment subsequently withdrawn, including last part of commission

indicators.note: including says one piece is put inside the other
withdrawn means drawn back, so the word for subsequently runs backwards

parts.note: later means subsequently

indicators.note: the final letter of the word commission is taken

explanation.surface: A fee later cancelled, though it included part of a commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' turns LATER into RETAL, and 'including' puts N (from 'last part of commission') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the sum paid to hire property, so it is a kind of payment.

clue.text: Story about equine female from Scotland

indicators.note: the story goes about, i.e. around, the equine

parts.note: a lie is a story, as in a fib
an ass is an equine animal, related to the horse

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl telling a tale about a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scots word for a girl, so it means a young female from Scotland.

clue.text: Hunting dog heading for big, big bird

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A hound making a beeline for a large bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The beagle is a small hound breed used for hunting hares, so it is an example of a hunting dog.

clue.text: Undecided where one might throw a ball?

definitions.meaning: a matter ... is not yet settled

definitions.text: where one might throw a ball?
definitions.meaning: a ball thrown upward goes literally up into the air

explanation.surface: Someone unsure about where to toss a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an unresolved matter is also the literal place a thrown ball ends up, overhead.

clue.text: Phone group of criminals?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a gang, as in a smuggling ...

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether to call the police about a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring is both a verb for telephoning and a noun for an organised gang of crooks.

clue.text: Some perch, a remarkable fish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An angler admiring a remarkable perch, itself a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The char is a trout-like freshwater fish of cold northern lakes.

clue.text: Cut on outside by blade reversed, so accurate

indicators.note: reversed says the word for a blade runs backwards

parts.note: an axe has a blade, standing here for it

indicators.note: the outside of the word cut is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A precise cut made by turning a blade round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns AXE into EXA; 'on outside' takes CT from 'Cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and accurate are synonyms meaning precise and without error.

clue.text: Make lace: stuff of poor quality

definitions.meaning: to make lace by hand-knotting thread

explanation.surface: Someone making lace from cheap materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is a verb for the craft of tatting lace and also slang for shoddy junk.

clue.text: Sticky stuff, plate fairly edible?

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: A sticky plateful that might just about be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a cryptic definition: food that is goodish is fairly good, so passably edible.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodish means fairly good or passable, so of food it suggests reasonably edible.

clue.text: Ghost creeps eerily round back of apartment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the single letter
eerily means in a weird way, so the letters are rearranged weirdly
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A ghost creeping eerily around the rear of a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is an apparition or phantom, a synonym for ghost.

clue.text: Composer left in temper when rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards
the abbreviation for left sits in the word for temper

parts.note: rage is temper, as in a fit of anger

explanation.surface: A composer left in a fury after being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside RAGE to give RAGLE, which 'when rejected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was an English composer, known for the Enigma Variations.
